svg.title: Choosing a Data Model in Microsoft Fabric: Technique, Store, and Read Mode
svg.desc: A three-gate decision tree. Gate 1 asks what the model must optimise for: BI query simplicity branches to a dimensional star schema, while auditable history across many volatile sources branches to data vault. Gate 2 asks which engine owns writes: Spark and multi-format engineering branches to a Lakehouse over managed Delta tables, T-SQL with multi-table transactions branches to a Warehouse — both converge on gate 3. Gate 3 asks how the semantic model should read the conformed table, decided per table: Direct Lake for large fresh facts, Import for compact fully-modellable tables, DirectQuery or composite for source-authoritative or exception tables. A warning node reached only from the Direct Lake branch flags that basing a Direct Lake on SQL table on a SQL view forces every query into DirectQuery fallback, and that fallback traffic lands on the DirectQuery branch anyway.
svg.text: Choosing a data model in Microsoft Fabric
Three separable decisions, in order: modelling technique → physical store → semantic read mode (decided per table)

g.aria-label: Gate 1: What must the model optimise for?
g.title: Gate 1 — What must the model optimise for? — The root question: choose the modelling technique from the job the model has to do, not from habit.
g.text: What must the model optimise for?
BI query simplicity, or auditable history across many volatile sources — pick the technique from the job, not from habit.

svg.text: BI query simplicity is the priority

g.title: Dimensional / star schema — Facts at a declared grain plus conformed dimensions; the default when BI query simplicity is the goal.
g.text: facts at a declared grain + conformed dims
Best when the consumer is BI and query
Heuristic: a fact table >~50 columns is

g.title: Data vault — Hubs, links, satellites — used only when auditable history across many volatile sources is the actual requirement.
g.text: Use only when auditable history across
many volatile sources is the requirement.
Never queried directly by BI — a dimensional
layer is still built on top for reporting.

svg.text: star schema ready for a physical store

g.aria-label: Gate 2: Which engine owns the writes?
g.title: Gate 2 — Which engine owns the writes? — Lakehouse or Warehouse, decided by engine and transaction needs, not by storage format.
g.text: Both stores persist Delta — decide by Spark vs T-SQL and whether multi-table transactions are required.

g.title: Lakehouse (Spark over managed Delta) — Spark-native engineering over managed Delta tables; the Bronze/Silver home in the recommended medallion split.
g.text: Spark over managed Delta · SQL analytics endpoint (read)
Recommended for Bronze/Silver Spark ETL, CDC, feature
engineering; Gold optionally built here as materialized views.
Watch: SQL analytics endpoint is read-oriented, not a write target.

g.title: Warehouse (T-SQL, multi-table ACID) — Full T-SQL surface with multi-table transactions over Delta; the recommended home for a Gold star schema with procedural logic.
g.text: T-SQL over open Delta · stored procedures
Recommended for a Gold star schema with multi-table
ACID loads; reads Lakehouse Silver via cross-database query.
Watch: cross-database perf degrades if Lakehouse-side files aren't compacted.

svg.text: conformed Delta table ready for a semantic model
GATE 3 · SEMANTIC READ MODE — DECIDE PER TABLE

g.aria-label: Gate 3: How should the semantic model read it?
g.title: Gate 3 — How should the semantic model read it? — Third question, decided per table: Direct Lake, Import, or DirectQuery/composite.
g.text: How should the semantic model read it?
Composite models let this be decided per table — not once for the whole model.

g.title: Direct Lake — Delta columns read directly from OneLake; best fit for large, fresh fact tables with no import refresh.
g.text: No scheduled import refresh; best fit for
large fact tables where freshness matters.
faster) or on SQL (endpoint security / fallback).
↓ risk: table mapped to a SQL view

g.title: Import — Copied into semantic-model memory; best fit for compact, fully-modellable tables.
g.text: flexibility; best for compact, curated tables.
Still used deliberately alongside Direct Lake

g.title: DirectQuery / composite — Forwards queries to the source, or mixes modes per table; best fit for source-authoritative or exception tables.
g.text: forward queries, or mix modes per table
query-time source latency, no refresh window.
from a Direct Lake table lands here too.

svg.text: table mapped to a SQL view, not a base table

g.aria-label: Trap: SQL view forces DirectQuery fallback
g.title: Trap: SQL view forces DirectQuery fallback — In Direct Lake on SQL, a table based on a SQL view sends every query into DirectQuery fallback.
g.text: Trap: SQL view forces DirectQuery fallback
In Direct Lake on SQL, mapping a model table to a SQL analytics-endpoint view — instead of a base table —
forces every query against it into DirectQuery fallback, usually slower and invisible on the surface.
Fix: map to base tables; materialize any needed view logic and remove non-deterministic functions from it.

svg.text: Fabric Atlas — original diagram, July 2026. Not a Microsoft asset; item icons vendored under Microsoft's Fabric icon terms.
